# nish/net/http1-codec

An incremental HTTP/1.1 request parser and a response writer, sans-IO: bytes in, events and bytes out, and no socket anywhere.

```ts
import {
  HTTP1_BODY,
  HTTP1_CHUNKED,
  HTTP1_CLOSED,
  HTTP1_END,
  HTTP1_ERROR,
  HTTP1_FIRST_HEAD,
  HTTP1_FIRST_INPUT,
  HTTP1_HEAD,
  HTTP1_MAX_METHOD,
  HTTP1_NEED_MORE,
  HTTP1_NO_BODY,
  HTTP1_NO_ROOM,
  HTTP1_REFUSED,
  HTTP1_UPGRADE,
  Http1Parser,
  http1BytesAre,
  http1Chunk,
  http1HexValue,
  http1IsFieldText,
  http1IsOws,
  http1IsToken,
  http1IsTokenByte,
  http1IsValueByte,
  http1LastChunk,
  http1PutText,
  http1ResponseHead,
  http1SameWord,
  http1Text,
  http1WriteChunk,
  http1WriteLastChunk,
  http1WriteResponseHead,
} from "nish/net/http1-codec";
```

```ts
import { Http1Parser, HTTP1_HEAD, HTTP1_BODY, HTTP1_END, HTTP1_ERROR } from "nish/net/http1-codec";

const p = new Http1Parser(maxTarget, maxHeaderBytes, maxHeaders, maxBody);
p.feed(received, 0, n);
let event: i32 = p.next();
while (event !== HTTP1_NEED_MORE) {
  // HTTP1_HEAD: p.method, p.target, p.header("host"), ...
  // HTTP1_BODY: p.body[p.bodyOff .. p.bodyOff + p.bodyLen)
  // HTTP1_ERROR: answer p.status and close
  event = p.next();
}
```

<scalar-callout type="info">

**The parser** is a push-pull machine. A caller `feed`s whatever slice the
socket gave it, of any length and cut anywhere, and then calls `next()`
until it answers `HTTP1_NEED_MORE`:

</scalar-callout>

The events are `HTTP1_HEAD` (the request line and header section are in),
`HTTP1_BODY` (some body bytes, de-chunked), `HTTP1_END` (the message is
complete; with keep-alive the next request follows), `HTTP1_UPGRADE` (the
request asked to switch protocols and has ended: the bytes after it are not
HTTP), `HTTP1_CLOSED` (the request said `Connection: close`, so nothing
after it is read) and `HTTP1_ERROR` (with the status to answer in `status`).
The last three repeat on every later call. Only complete lines are acted on
and body bytes are counted, never guessed, so the sequence of heads, the
concatenated body and the final event do not depend on where the input was
cut — `tests/link/net_http1_split` feeds a corpus at every split point.

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**What it refuses, and with what** (RFC 9112 unless named):

- 400: a malformed request line or field line; a bare LF or a stray CR
  (§2.2); whitespace before the first field or an obs-fold (§2.2, §5.2);
  whitespace between a field name and its colon (§5.1); a field value with a
  control character; a 1.1 request without exactly one `Host`, or a 1.0
  request with more than one (§3.2, RFC 9110 §7.2); `Content-Length` that is
  not one run of digits, or that appears twice (§6.3); `Transfer-Encoding`
  together with `Content-Length`, in a 1.0 request, or whose last coding is
  not `chunked` (§6.1, §6.3); a malformed chunk size, chunk extension or
  chunk terminator (§7.1). These are the request-smuggling shapes, and each
  one is refused rather than repaired, because two parsers that repair one
  differently disagree on where the next request starts.
- 413: a declared or a de-chunked body longer than `maxBody`.
- 414: a request target longer than `maxTarget`.
- 431: a header (or trailer) section longer than `maxHeaderBytes`, or with
  more than `maxHeaders` fields.
- 501: a transfer coding other than `chunked` (§6.1).
- 505: an HTTP major version other than 1. A 1.x minor version above 1 is
  read as 1.1, as RFC 9110 §6.2 asks.

</scalar-callout>

An error is final: the parser answers `HTTP1_ERROR` from then on and
ignores further input, and the caller answers `status` and closes. Every
limit is the caller's number. A method is at most `HTTP1_MAX_METHOD` bytes.

<scalar-detail title="Connection management">

`keepAlive` is true for a 1.1 request unless
`Connection` lists `close`, and for a 1.0 request only when it lists
`keep-alive` (§9.3). `upgrade` is the `Upgrade` field's value when a 1.1
request also lists `upgrade` in `Connection`, and empty otherwise (RFC 9110
§7.8 says a 1.0 request's `Upgrade` is ignored). After such a request's
`HTTP1_END` the parser stops at `HTTP1_UPGRADE`; `upgradeBytes()` answers
what was fed past the request, for the next protocol, and `declineUpgrade()`
goes back to HTTP for a server that answered without switching.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The writer">

**The writer** is `http1ResponseHead`, which answers a status line and
header section with the framing field the body needs, and `http1Chunk` and
`http1LastChunk` for a chunked body. It refuses (`null`) anything that would
let a caller's string end a line early — the response-splitting shape.
`http1WriteResponseHead` writes the same head into a caller's buffer with
nothing allocated, and adds a `Date` field from the bytes it is given
(`httpDateWrite` in `nish/net/http-fields` makes them) to a final response.

</scalar-detail>

Field names are kept in lowercase, the form RFC 9110 §5.1 says they compare
in and the form HTTP/2 sends them in. Strings in the language are bytes, so a
field value holding obs-text (0x80 to 0xFF) arrives byte for byte.

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

Written from RFC 9112 and RFC 9110, not ported from another implementation.

## http1Chunk

`data[off .. off + len)` as one chunk of a chunked body, in an array of its
own; `http1WriteChunk` writes the same bytes into a buffer the caller owns.
An empty window answers an empty array, because a chunk of size zero is the
end of the body and only `http1LastChunk` writes that. A window outside
`data` panics.

```ts
function http1Chunk(
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
```

## http1ResponseHead

An HTTP/1.1 status line and header section (RFC 9112 §4, §5), ending in
the empty line, with the framing field `bodyLength` asks for appended:
`Content-Length: n` for `n >= 0`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` for
`HTTP1_CHUNKED`, and neither for `HTTP1_NO_BODY`.

Answers `null`, and writes nothing, for a status outside 100 to 599; a
reason phrase or field value holding CR, LF or another control character
(which would end the line early and let the rest be read as a field or a
second response); a field name that is not a token; `names` and `values` of
different lengths; a `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding` among the
caller's fields, since the framing is decided here; a 1xx or 204 response
with a body length (RFC 9110 §15.2, §15.3.5); and any other `bodyLength`
below zero.

```ts
function http1ResponseHead(
  status: i32,
  reason: string,
  names: string[],
  values: string[],
  bodyLength: i32,
): u8[] | null
```

## http1WriteChunk

Writes `data[off .. off + len)` as one chunk of a chunked body (RFC 9112
§7.1) into `out` at `at` — the size in lowercase hex, CRLF, the bytes,
CRLF — and answers where it ends, or `HTTP1_NO_ROOM` when it does not fit,
with `out` untouched. An empty window writes nothing and answers `at`,
because a chunk of size zero ends the body. A window outside `data` panics.

```ts
function http1WriteChunk(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  data: readonly u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): i32
```

## http1WriteResponseHead

`http1ResponseHead`'s status line and header section, written into `out`
at `at` with nothing allocated: field names and values are octets (as
`nish/net/http-fields` holds them), and `connection`, when not empty, is
sent as a `Connection` field after the caller's. `date`, when not empty, is
sent as a `Date` field between the caller's fields and the framing ones
(RFC 9110 §6.6.1), on a final status only, and not when the caller's fields
already hold a `date` in any case: the caller's wins, so a response carries
one. Answers where the head ends; `HTTP1_REFUSED` for everything
`http1ResponseHead` refuses, a `Connection` among the caller's fields when
`connection` is given, a `connection` that is not field text, and a `date`
that is not field text on a final status, the only one it is sent on;
`HTTP1_NO_ROOM` when it is well formed but does not fit, the `Date` line
counted when it is sent. Either way `out` is untouched.

```ts
function http1WriteResponseHead(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  status: i32,
  reason: string,
  names: u8[][],
  values: u8[][],
  bodyLength: i32,
  connection: string,
  date: u8[],
): i32
```

## Http1Parser

One connection's request parser, from the first byte to the close: requests
on a kept-alive connection follow one another through the same parser.

```ts
class Http1Parser
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http1Parser(maxTarget: i32, maxHeaderBytes: i32, maxHeaders: i32, maxBody: i32)` | Each limit is clamped into 0 to 2^30, so that the sums the parser makes of them (a request line is the method, the target and ten bytes more) cannot overflow an `i32`. |
| `body: u8[]` | The buffer the last `HTTP1_BODY`'s bytes are in, at `bodyOff`, `bodyLen` long. |
| `bodyLen: i32` |  |
| `bodyOff: i32` |  |
| `bodyTotal: i32` | De-chunked body bytes so far, against `maxBody`. |
| `buf: u8[]` | The bytes fed and not yet consumed are `buf[start .. end)`. |
| `chunked: boolean` |  |
| `contentLength: i32` | The declared body length, or -1 when the request has none or is chunked. |
| `end: i32` |  |
| `fieldCount: i32` | Field lines of the request so far, its trailers included, against `maxHeaders`. |
| `head: u8[]` | The request line and the kept field lines of the request, copied out of `buf` as each is read, names in lowercase: what the spans below index. Kept from one request to the next, so a slot that has seen its largest head allocates nothing for the next one. |
| `headerCount: i32` | How many fields the request's header section kept: the spans of field `i` are `spans[4 * i ..]`. |
| `headHeld: boolean` | Whether a kept-alive request ended and its head is still held for the response: the next `next()` clears it before it reads a byte more. |
| `headLength: i32` | How much of `head` the request uses. |
| `keepAlive: boolean` |  |
| `keepText: boolean` | Whether `method`, `target`, `names`, `values` and `upgrade` are filled as strings. A server that must allocate nothing per request turns it off and reads the head through `head`, the spans and the `...Is` methods. |
| `left: i32` | Bytes left in a length-delimited body or in the current chunk. |
| `lineControl: boolean` | Whether the line being scanned holds a byte a field value may not: a control byte other than HTAB, or DEL (RFC 9110 §5.5). `http1TakeLine` sets it as it looks for the line's end, so a field line's bytes are read once, not once for the LF and again for the check. |
| `lineEnd: i32` |  |
| `lineStart: i32` | The line `http1TakeLine` found is `buf[lineStart .. lineEnd)`, its CRLF dropped. |
| `maxBody: i32` |  |
| `maxChunk: i32` | The most body bytes one `HTTP1_BODY` hands over; a caller's number, 2^30 unless set. |
| `maxHeaderBytes: i32` |  |
| `maxHeaders: i32` |  |
| `maxTarget: i32` |  |
| `method: string` |  |
| `methodEnd: i32` |  |
| `methodStart: i32` | The method is `head[methodStart .. methodEnd)` and the target `head[targetStart .. targetEnd)`. |
| `minor: i32` | The minor version: 0 for HTTP/1.0, 1 for HTTP/1.1 and anything above it. |
| `names: string[]` | The field names, in lowercase, in the order they arrived; `values` beside them. |
| `reason: string` | What was wrong, once `next()` said `HTTP1_ERROR`; for a log, not for the response. |
| `scan: i32` | Where the search for the next LF resumes, so a line fed a byte at a time is scanned once. |
| `sectionBytes: i32` | Bytes of the header or trailer section so far, against `maxHeaderBytes`. |
| `spans: i32[]` | Four entries per field, into `head`: name start and end, value start and end (OWS trimmed). |
| `start: i32` |  |
| `state: i32` |  |
| `status: i32` | The status code to answer once `next()` said `HTTP1_ERROR`. |
| `tally: Http1ListTally` | Reused by every list `http1Tally` walks. |
| `target: string` |  |
| `targetEnd: i32` |  |
| `targetStart: i32` |  |
| `upgrade: string` | The `Upgrade` field when `Connection` asked for it, else empty. |
| `upgrading: boolean` | Whether the request asked to switch protocols (`upgrade` is its value when `keepText`). |
| `values: string[]` |  |
| `buffered(): i32` | How many bytes were fed and not consumed yet: what a caller bounds its reads by. |
| `declineUpgrade(): void` | After `HTTP1_UPGRADE`: the server answered without switching, so the bytes that follow are the next HTTP request. Anywhere else it does nothing. |
| `feed(data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Appends `data[off .. off + len)` to the input. A window outside `data` panics, as the crypto modules' `update` does. Once the parser has closed or refused, the input is dropped; once it has upgraded, it is kept for `upgradeBytes()`. |
| `header(name: string): string \| null` | The value of the first field named `name` (any case), or `null`. A field that may repeat is read through the spans. The answer is a fresh string; `headerIndex` and `headerIs` allocate nothing. |
| `headerIndex(name: string): i32` | The index of the first field named `name` (any case), or -1. |
| `headerIs(name: string, value: string): boolean` | Whether the first field named `name` (any case) has exactly the value `value`. |
| `methodIs(text: string): boolean` | Whether the method is exactly `text` (methods are case-sensitive, RFC 9110 §9.1). |
| `next(): i32` | The next event the input holds; see the module comment. |
| `restart(): void` | Puts the parser back as the constructor left it, for the next connection, keeping every buffer it has grown: a slot that is reused allocates nothing to start over. |
| `resting(): boolean` | Whether the parser waits for a request line with nothing fed and unread, so its input and head buffers hold nothing it needs: a caller may lend them out and leave empty arrays in `buf`, `body` and `head`, which the next feed and head make or the caller puts back first. |
| `targetIs(text: string): boolean` | Whether the request target is exactly `text`. |
| `upgradeBytes(): u8[]` | After `HTTP1_UPGRADE`: every byte fed past the request, as a fresh array. |
| `upgradeIs(protocol: string): boolean` | Whether the request asked to switch to exactly `protocol` (any case): one `Upgrade` field holding that one token, with `upgrade` in `Connection`. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="32" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_MAX_METHOD: i32`

The longest method this parser reads; a longer one is a 400.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_BODY: i32`

`next()`: `bodyLen` body bytes are at `body[bodyOff ..]`, valid until the next `feed`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_CHUNKED: i32`

`http1ResponseHead`'s `bodyLength` for a chunked body.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_CLOSED: i32`

`next()`, from now on: the request closed the connection; nothing more is read.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_END: i32`

`next()`: the request's body is complete. Its head (method, target,
version, fields, `keepAlive`) still reads as this request's until the next
call to `next()`, so a response written at `HTTP1_END` sees the request it
answers and never the pipelined one behind it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_ERROR: i32`

`next()`, from now on: the input is refused; `status` and `reason` say why.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="256" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_FIRST_HEAD: i32`

The head buffer a parser makes for its first head.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1,024" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_FIRST_INPUT: i32`

The input buffer a parser makes on its first feed, the smallest it grows from.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_HEAD: i32`

`next()`: a request line and header section were read.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_NEED_MORE: i32`

`next()`: the input so far holds no further event; feed more.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_NO_BODY: i32`

`http1ResponseHead`'s `bodyLength` for a response that carries no body field (1xx, 204, 304, HEAD).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_NO_ROOM: i32`

`http1WriteResponseHead` and `http1WriteChunk`: the bytes do not fit at `at`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_REFUSED: i32`

`http1WriteResponseHead`: a head the writer refuses to write.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_UPGRADE: i32`

`next()`, from now on: the request switched protocols; see `upgradeBytes()`.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
